cohort: 2,059,578 non-malformed singleton live-births in Sweden born 1983-2004
finding: Very/extremely preterm birth, caesarean section birth, and small-for-gestational age at birth were associated with an increased risk of bipolar disorder in offspring.
mod_finding: Compared with vaginal birth, caesarean section birth was associated with 1.20 (1.08, 1.33) and 1.58 (1.06, 2.36) times higher bipolar disorder risk in general and sibling cohorts, respectively.
